desc:
You walk from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell of grid, stepping only right or down. The sum of all cell values on a route (including both end cells) is the route's score.

Count the routes whose score is divisible by k. Since the count may be enormous, return it modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: Only the remainder of the running sum modulo k matters, never the sum itself.
Extend the usual path-counting DP with a third dimension: ways[r][c][x] is the number of routes to (r, c) whose sum leaves remainder x.
A route reaching (r, c) with remainder x comes from above or from the left with remainder (x - grid[r][c]) mod k. The answer is ways[m-1][n-1][0].
editorial: Two routes that arrive at the same cell with the same remainder modulo k are indistinguishable for the rest of the journey, so we can merge them into one counter. The state is therefore (cell, remainder), giving at most 50 · 50 · 50 states.

Transition: after stepping onto a cell of value v, a route that had remainder x in its predecessor now has remainder (x + v) mod k. Add the counters of the upper and left predecessors under that shift, taking the result modulo 109+7. Seed the top-left cell with remainder grid[0][0] mod k equal to 1. Only the previous row and the current row of remainder tables are needed, so memory is O(n · k) and time is O(m · n · k).
